Easiest to hardest, based on my own observations as a healer... a traditional tank > a damage-focused tank > a hybrid tank.

The traditional tank is the typical "Wall" tank. They keep enemies focused on them and generally take fairly low damage. They also do very little damage themselves. Their cooldowns are often just a bonus in non-raid settings, but they are the most durable.

Before the hybrid tank emerged, the damage-focused tank was the go-to for dealing damage. Now, they serve as a balanced option. They don't deal as much damage as the hybrid tank, but they also don't take as much damage. They aren't as durable as the traditional tank, but they inflict more damage. Damage-focused tanks excel at area-of-effect threat generation and self-sustain. They **will** take damage, but they have tools to recover. You need to understand your cooldowns fairly well to play a damage-focused tank, but you can survive even with some mismanagement.

The hybrid tank... oh the hybrid tank. I dread seeing them in random groups right now, even as I approach a higher level. A hybrid tank will have many of the strengths of damage-focused tanks, but even stronger. Their area-of-effect pulling is exceptional. They essentially get a combination of a traditional tank's area threat generation (which does no damage) and a damage-focused tank's area threat generation (which does damage), allowing them to surround themselves with threat while dealing damage. Hybrid tanks need to manage numerous aspects simultaneously, and if you let anything slip... well, you better hope your healer has some powerful healing abilities ready. It's not uncommon for me to need to spam my healing spells and use my strongest healing ability on a hybrid tank for most of a run's trash encounters. Hybrid tanks need to know precisely what they are doing at all times or they will get overwhelmed just as quickly as a high-damage class.

Story is the big thing here. A popular MMORPG has next to zero story to guide you... you just run zone to zone and collect things for people. In this game, your story will have you kill a literal embodiment of a god *within the first 15 hours of playtime*.

There's no "hybrid" classes (except one, but even they can't effectively heal as a damage dealer or deal damage as a healer). Healers are expected to deal damage (and given tools to effectively do so) during lower periods of damage in order to kill things faster (which, in some cases, is necessary to kill things at all).

All three tank classes feel unique enough, but can do everything effectively. One class's strength is survival while their weakness is damage. Another class's strength is aggro while their weakness is survival. The last class's strength is damage while their weakness is survival as well. The second class is probably the most well-rounded of the tanks, while the first class is the most simple and forgiving.

Overall, "raiding" is much easier to pick up and leave than the other game. You don't have to wait an hour between bosses killing meaningless henchmen.

With enough ability power, the second item procs can get downright silly (with certain high ability power items, the character could easily have 600 ability power, or a 300 damage nuke every 1.5 seconds), but a lot of the value of the first item comes from the chasing you get from a specific component.
